chapter: Billy Berg's band with Lee and Lester Young
title: Billy Berg's big band at the Capri and the Trouville
summary: Billy Berg hired him for a group with Slim and Slam, Lee and Lester Young and the Spirits of Rhythm, first at the Capri and then at the Trouville.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And finally, I got a call from Billy Berg. He wanted me to join a band with a Slim and Slam, and Lee and Lester Young, Bumps Meyers, and Jake Porter and Eddie Beal, the

Spirits of Rhythm -- a great big conglomeration thing. And he was going to pay forty dollars a week or something like that. Which was great with me. I mean, I'd be having fun. So I took it. And I worked out there...

We worked in a place called the Capri. And we had Big Joe Turner singin' the Blues, and Ray Bryant was dancing, and we traded off sets, you know, with Lee and Lester Young and Slim and Sam's band, alternating with Spirits of Rhythm with Teddy Bunn and Leo Watson, and Big Joe Turner was singing with them... I got to know an awful lot of people. Ben Webster used to come in. I had met Ben previously in Seattle, and we became very close, and he used to come out there all the time and play with us. And he kept telling me, you know, he says, "I'm gonna get you with Benny Goodman if it's the last thing I do." And he did. He got his chance.

We switched clubs, and moved down to Fairfax and Beverly into a place called the Trouville, and they changed everything all around. It became Lee and Lester Young's band without Slim and Sam. That's where I met Red Callender and Louis Gonzales, a guitar player, and a trumpet player from St. Louis who used to be with Basie, Paul Campbell, and Lester and Bumps, Lee, and me -- we were the band.
